kind_note: Autonomous theorem prover that writes formal Lean proofs; an internal research system whose outputs (proofs) Axiom Math has released, not a shipped product. Lab note 'harness' is not accurate.
note: No public release found. Axiom's introductory post (https://axiommath.ai/research/from-seeing-why-to-checking-everything, dated January 8, 2026) says 'Over our first few months we have been building AxiomProver, an autonomous AI theorem prover that produces formal Lean proofs to mathematical problems' and 'Today, we release the proofs generated by AxiomProver', and 'A technical report on AxiomProver is to follow.' It does not say the system itself is available to anyone. The only public product found is AXLE, Axiom's separate Lean engine/API (announced March 5, 2026, https://axiommath.ai/research/releasing-axle); AXLE is not AxiomProver. An AI wiki entry (https://aiwiki.ai/wiki/axiomprover) says AxiomProver was not publicly released as of August 19, 2026, with no source code, checkpoints, API or pricing published; I could not open that page (HTTP 429), so this rests on a secondary source plus absence of any availability announcement. A third-party directory lists 'Public API access' for Axiom Math; I did not verify it and it appears to refer to AXLE. Latest dated item found: August 17, 2026 (Lean proof of the 246 prime-gap bound). Unsettled: whether a technical report or limited access was later announced after the searches.
